headline: Election Shake-Up and Gulf Tensions Frame a Cautious Open After a Chip-Led, Mixed Tuesday
body_html:
U.S. markets open Wednesday with politics and the Gulf both on the tape. Democrats swept key races in the midterm elections, and early reports describe a rout for Republicans. Oil is firmer on uncertainty around the Iran conflict, while gold is higher as the dollar softens.

The backdrop is a split session. On Tuesday, 250 stocks in our 526-stock universe rose and 272 fell. Semiconductors jumped 3.29% and industrials added 0.44%, but homebuilders sank 3.68% and consumer names lost 1.17%. Fabrinet climbed 15.45%, while Dynatrace dropped 14.69% and Gartner fell 13.19%.

At the open, watch whether chip strength carries over after such a sharp move, and whether homebuilders find a floor. Software, down 0.67% Tuesday, faces a test after heavy losses at Dynatrace and Shopify. Gulf news also bears watching: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says four tankers caught fire after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz, even as Trump told the Financial Times there is no immediate plan to strike Iran. Block, which raised its outlook, is also on the radar.

briefs.headline: Democrats Sweep Midterm Contests
briefs.body: Reports describe a broad Democratic win in the midterm elections, with the party holding a New Hampshire Senate seat. Analysts are weighing what a shift in Washington means for trade policy and the Iran conflict, and early reaction in Asia has been hopeful about relief.

briefs.headline: Oil and Gold Both Firmer Overnight
briefs.body: Crude is higher as traders weigh uncertainty over the Iran war after the Republican setback at the polls. Gold is also rising, helped by a weaker dollar as Democrats picked up early wins. Both moves point to a defensive tone ahead of the open.

briefs.headline: Tankers Burn Near Hormuz
briefs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says four tankers are ablaze after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, India says one of its citizens died in an attack on a ship near Oman. Shipping risk in the Gulf remains a key swing factor for energy.

briefs.headline: Washington Says No Strike Planned for Now
briefs.body: Trump told the Financial Times the U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran, a calming note against a tense maritime backdrop. He also acknowledged Iran's role in the Democratic sweep. Traders will look for any shift in tone through the day.

briefs.headline: Chip and Power Names Led Tuesday
briefs.body: Semiconductors gained 3.29% as a group, the strongest sector in our universe. Fabrinet rose 15.45%, FormFactor 10.87% and Advanced Energy 9.63%. The open will show whether buyers keep chasing after such sharp gains or take profits.

briefs.headline: Software and Research Names Hit Hard
briefs.body: Dynatrace fell 14.69%, Gartner 13.19%, Shopify 8.74% and HealthStream 8.42% on Tuesday, dragging software down 0.67%. Homebuilders were the weakest group, off 3.68%. Block adds a counterpoint today after lifting its profit outlook and reaching a preliminary Justice Department settlement.
